title: I Let the Harp-Studio Pedal Clock Catch the Mentor Who Camped My Numbered Disc

parts.text: I stepped into studio B at 5:04 p.m. and mentor Inez was already using numbered gear. The board said: ONE HARP. SIXTY MINUTES. DISCS STAY WITH THE SLOT. I was twenty-nine, studio secretary, holding a checkout that listed our numbered discs. Inez shrugged. "Mentors are the pedals." I photographed the board, the booking, and her leftover felts on my numbered disc. Then I asked for the pedal log. At 5:12 the desk pinged why Inez's name was on my felts. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The desk can see Inez's leftover felts on my numbered disc.

social.video_title: She camped my numbered harp disc on my slot — Part 1/2
social.description: Harp studio, leftover felts, a sixty-minute clock she posted. I logged the pedals. Would you have asked for the pedal log?

parts.text: Inez called it warm-up glisses until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the felt still. The discs went back to my numbered slot. Inez ran a slot of her own and told the next mentor atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: MENTORS ARE NOT THE PEDALS. I keep my discs on a labeled rack. Inez brown-bags her glisses. The studio finally looks like a slot, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Mentors are not the pedals — Part 2/2
social.description: Pedal log, numbered disc, and a second line on the board. Was a warm-up gliss ever my felts?
